items.title: Worse Together: How Performance Breaks Down in Multi-User Multi-Agent Teams
items.summary_1line: Worse Together: How Performance Breaks Down in Multi-User Multi-Agent Teams
items.editor_note: 첫 번째 실패 원인 분석 항목: 여러 에이전트로 구성된 팀이 여러 사용자를 응대할 때 발생하는 성능 저하 문제.

editorial.tldr: This is a research thread, not one event: three unrelated items about how teams of LLM agents perform. On Oct 29 the EvoTeam paper proposed evolving the team itself instead of tuning individual agents, and an Oct 30 explainer drew lessons from YC's Minecraft and Mindustry agent swarms.
editorial.whats_new: A Nov 12 post on Anthropic's alignment site, "Worse Together", examines how performance breaks down in multi-agent teams that serve multiple users, the thread's first item focused on failure.
editorial.why_it_matters: The first two items treat adding agents as a way to gain capability; the newest treats team composition, with more than one user in the loop, as a source of degradation to measure.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before adding agents or sharing one agent team across users, run the same eval against a single-agent, single-user baseline and compare. Read "Worse Together" for the breakdown conditions it reports before choosing a team topology.

beats.headline: "Worse Together" studies how multi-user multi-agent teams break down
beats.summary: A post on Anthropic's alignment site turns the thread from building teams to measuring where they lose performance.

open_questions: Which conditions in "Worse Together" cause the breakdown: more agents, more users, or conflicting instructions between users?
Does "Worse Together" report a mitigation, or only the degradation?
Does EvoTeam beat a strong single-agent baseline at equal token cost?
Do the game-swarm results from Minecraft and Mindustry carry over to software or data tasks?
